pr_title: Add support for PoE control of TP-Link Omada Gateways
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Adding control of PoE ports on integrated Omada Gateway+Switch devices like the ER7212PC.

Annoyingly, this required a bit more rework than I expected because PoE control is a port configuration API, whereas the other control switches act on the port status API. While I was doing this, I brought the Network Switch PoE controls in to the same Entity Description based entity to reduce duplication. That meant adding bit more generic type magic than I would ideally like.

issue_context.title: TP-Link Omada integrations does not support PoE on gateways
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Thanks for this great integration! While the integration seems to support enabling/disabling Power over Ethernet on a per-port basis for network switches this is not possible for Power over Ethernet ports on gateways. 
I have the ER7212 which has PoE ports which via the (integrated) Omada controller can be enabled/disabled on a per-port basis. Since this is already supported for switches I  wonder if it should not also work for this switch which is integrated in the gateway?

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.9.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

tplink_omada

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tplink_omada/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
No
```


### Additional information

Using the python tplink-omada-client I have obtained the dump file for the command

`omada gateway --dump`

The output is attached here.
[gateway_redacted.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/12724839/gateway_redacted.txt)

Ok, there are some instructions here that will help get more information from your particular devices that will help us decode the API they use add support for them.

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/89051#issuecomment-1509865062

Basically, you need to use the python `omada` command line client to dump the raw API information. With that, I can try to make sure the PoE ports are discovered in Home Assistant.

Please make sure you use the latest Omada controller firmware. For the combined switch/gateway device, I guess the command you will need will be `omada gateway --dump` but it's possible that it will show up as both a gateway and a switch, I'm not really sure. For the TL-SG3428XMP, I think it should appear in the switches output. Please also get the output for the `switch_ports` command, e.g. `omada switch_ports "Main Switch" --dump`.

If you upgrade to the latest version of `tplink-omada-client` command line (with `pip install --upgrade tplink-omada-client`) you should be able to see PoE status on the gateway's LAN ports.

The bad news is the ER7212PC doesn't seem to support disabling PoE on a per-port basis - at least I haven't seen the option in any of the review videos I have watched. If you can't do it via the management interface, it won't be possible to do it via the API either. Can you double-check that what you are asking for is possible in with the Omada interface?

I can probably add binary sensors to show which ports are providing power, if that would be useful?

Ok, thanks for the info. It looks like the device presents itself as just a gateway, and not a switch via the API.

So the question we have to answer is what does the API call look like to enable/disable PoE on a port. The TP-Link documentation doesn't go that deep, unfortunately.

If you don't mind getting your hands dirty in the F12 developer tools of Chrome (or the browser of your choice...) it would be great if you could capture the API call that the controller makes when it enables/disables PoE on a particular port. Normally, it's quite easy to find the call...

It will likely be a POST or PATCH request to a URL, which I'm guessing will look something like `/{xxxxxxxx}/api/v2/gateways/{mac}/poeSettings/{port_id}` (so it will probably show up as a file called "6" in the network log for toggling port 6). I guess it will have a payload something like `{ "portId": n, "enable": 1 }`.

I'll need the URL, the Method (e.g. POST) and the payload. If you can find out what this request looks like, I can add a function for it in the API as a first step. Adding the feature to HA takes a little bit more effort, but we'll get there in the end.

All I have is a picture on the TP-Link website.
Once I update the integration to support the ports, it might be better to handle this just by renaming in HA. But if there is a consistent logical mapping, I can possibly normalise it in the API.

review_comments: Why can't we always write ha state and request a refresh or just always request a refresh?
Please put parentheses around the lambda and indent it so it's easier to separate it from the entity description parameters.
To understand it better: Can a user rename a port to a custom name?

For network switches, yes, ports can be renamed in the Omada controller. For gateways, no, the ports have numbers and fixed names like "WAN/LAN" that aren't visible via the API. Just another inconsistency in the Omada ecosystem. Gateways and Switches have a wildly different API behind the scenes.
This kind of logic is an anti pattern when using entity descriptions. I'd pass both enable and port details and put a default for `update_func` that just returns enable.
